Gift of the givers - How to save a life

By: Floris Kotze | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Not your average NGO, this is the largest disaster response organisation on the continent.

Unique Selling Point:
An intimate look at Dr Imtiaz Sooliman, the founder of Gift of the Givers

Summary:
Treatment Overview
Opening and setup: 2 minutes
We start the insert with a collection of disasters, wars, earthquakes and water shortages. From there we go into a link - we hold the audience in suspense - we explain where we are. In Pietermaritzburg. The reason why we visit a seemingly ordinary town is for an extraordinary individual. All will be revealed soon.
Our presenter meets our hero. Dr Sooliman. Known for his NGO - Gift of the givers. We find ourselves in a warehouse. It’s massive. We conduct the interview in one of the main distribution centers of GOTG. We talk about Dr Sooliman’s history, from Potch to Maritzburg.
Gift of the Givers: 4 Minutes
Dr Sooliman is synonymous with Gift of the Givers. He has been all over the world, saving lives. Most recently, drilling hundreds of boreholes for the water crisis in the Eastern Cape. He talks to us about a variety of disasters his NGO was involved in. Lots of action and pace is fast.
Then
We find out GOTG is much more than we thought… We visit a school that GOTG built, the lives of children touched by the good doctor are evident here in a small school near Maritzburg.
But there’s more… We also see a medical center they built, to help the less fortunate. We see Dr Sooliman talk at another unveiling of a ward at the Charlotte Maxeke hospital in Joburg… He is a very busy man. We cover a lot of these with photos.
But then, we slow the pace again….

Faith: 2 Minutes
All of what he created was through his faith. It is one of the most important pillars of GOTG. We see him in an intimate prayer session, in a mosque. We now have a better understanding of this unique individual. Dr Sooliman is one of the special ones. It takes someone like him to change the course of history. What would have happened to the people he saved, if it was not for him. Making the decision to start Gift of the Givers, in 1992, was life-changing.

Closing: 2 minutes
We wind it down as we look at what has been achieved by Dr Sooliman. And yet, he doesn’t care about the lifetime achievement award or the recognition he gets from the Presidency. Gift of the givers is all about the people of this beautiful country of ours.


Further information:
Details of the insert
I want to approach this as a mini doccie. To showcase Dr Sooliman. It won’t be a plight for donations or an advert for Gift of the Givers, just a look at the life of Dr Sooliman and his legacy. The audience will connect with him immediately, clearly a no BS person. Someone that acts. By the end of the insert, we will feel inspired and much more positive about our country. Dr Sooliman will take us on a journey of hope.


Interviews: Dr Imtiaz Sooliman
Pietermaritzburg School Headmaster
Pietermaritzburg Clinic Nurse

Script:


Opening VO:
It's just after 7 o’clock in the morning, and the school run is in full swing...
Rahma is among the sea of children walking to school. As so many times before, her dad walks alongside her to the classroom.

7 year old Rahma, is completely unaware, that disaster follows his every step….

[Cut to dramatic video montage of wars, GOTG helping, showcasing GOTG but also a little bit of Dr Sooliman philanthropic endeavours]

LINK:
In my time working as a journalist in South Africa, I’ve seen the very worst and the very best of us… but few people embody the spirit of this country, like the man I set to meet today.
And you'll find him here in this industrial part of Pietermaritzburg…

Cut back to a calm morning as Lourensa meets Dr Sooliman at the gates of GOTG, we meet Dr Sooliman, we walk into the GOTG site, and he says, “Welcome to Gift of the Givers….
{We now know where we are… }

VO:
Dr Imtiaz Sooliman is a South African humanitarian, who founded the Gift of the Givers Foundation, in 1992. He gave up his successful medical practice, to follow a calling, resulting in this, the largest disaster response organisation of African origin, providing emergency relief & aid, to people affected by natural disasters, wars, and other crises in over 40 countries.
Much of the relief aid is sent from this warehouse.

Dr Sooliman
I never expected it to be so big. When you think of a small Muslim group in South Africa, how big are you going to be? You don't have that kind of big money where everybody from all races and all religions will participate. Where you have mixed teams going all across the world.







Lourensa
How big is the Organisation today?
Dr Sooliman
107 full time people in South Africa, probably 500 staff around the world. Gift of the Givers wasn’t my idea. It's totally spiritual. I met spiritual teacher in Turkey in 1992. The spiritual teacher just picks up his head, makes eye contact with me and looks heavenwards and in fluid Turkish and I don't speak a word of Turkish, he said my son I'm not asking you I'm instructing you to form an organisation and its name is in Arabic will be Waqful Waqifin - Gift of the Givers. You will serve people of all races, all religions, all colours, all classes, all cultures. You will expect nothing in return, not even a thank you. This is an instruction for you, for the rest of your life. Whatever you do, is done through you and not by you.

VO: 02m50s
After all these years, Dr. Sooliman continues to answer the call, to help those in need. The Gift of the Givers is involved in a wide variety of initiatives, from improving hospitals and schools to providing free mental health care. They rely entirely on donations in cash, or in kind….

LINK:
Many years ago this house was the headquarters of the gift of the givers day it's a refuge for people in the community in need of counselling and psychological support.

VO: 00:03:21.21
Heading up this programme is Gift of the Givers Co-founder and Dr Sooliman’s wife, Zohra Sooliman.

Zohra Sooliman:
There weren't any psychological support services for the Indian Muslim community and so that is why I decided okay let's start of this gift of the givers care-line counselling service. As much as I thought this was only for the Muslim and the Indian community it opened up to everybody and we also work in schools where we do lots of life skills and we do topics like anti-bullying, anger management, substance abuse.

Bijay Sewpersadh
Support from Gift of the Givers is so immense, we will really struggle to allow our children to reach the standard that they are without their support.



VO: 00:04:12:16
What was once a bare lifeless classroom, now bloomed with vibrant colours, offering a lifeline to the less fortunate children, who would have otherwise been deprived of such opportunities. This remarkable transformation owes much to Principal Sewpersadh's unwavering commitment to the school. He reached out to Dr. Sooliman for assistance.

Bijay Sewpersadh
Children who are dyslexic, have autism, for whatever reason they seem to be children of a Lesser God and support is missing, but when Doc and the foundation came along they saw this need for us to really support the vulnerable children. They come in with that compassion, that love. He is such an optimistic person. Where I would be struggling to find a way, he just brings this optimism and gives it to us and says, “here’s the way for you”.

Dr Sooliman
It’s all things that are doable, and you’re making a difference to somebody’s life. You can’t make a difference to 65 million people’s lives, but you can make a difference to one life. And every day you add a few more lives, and that’s what we believe in doing.

When you help the people you feel this peace, when you see a smile on a person's face or a child being happy or something, something happens in your soul, I can’t explain it. I find peace in my prayer. I find peace in my spiritual readings. Every time I need some arrangement or some network, it comes right in front of me. I need people, they call me, if I need something, I get to know about it. If something is about to happen, I made that connection three weeks before it happens. It all comes at the right time and the right place, it just placed in front for you. There's no doubt in thirty years that everything about this is spiritual.

VO: 00:06:13.18
Dr. Imtiaz Sooliman's selfless dedication over the last 3 decades, has saved millions of people, yet it has taken a profound toll on his own life.

The spiritual teacher told me specifically that when you do this job you got to divide your life into three parts, one part for yourself, one part for your family, and one part for what you gonna do. I could never follow that formula. Everything went, ‘cause I basically destroyed the family… and that’s the only regret that I have in my life, I have lost out on my children.


Zorah Sooliman:
In those areas which were the early years of my children, Imtiaz was away a lot of the time overseas for long and extended periods. I looked at myself as the one stable anchor in my children's life. Because Imtiaz was travelling so extensively, they need a semblance of a solid family. I wasn't going to compromise that at any cost. God has steered our parts in our life, but we've accepted that this is our life and with it comes a lot of sacrifices.

Lourensa:
And then you met your second wife?

Dr Sooliman:
Yes, I met her, after the earthquake in Pakistan in 2005 and then in 2007 December we got married.
The greatest joy is when I see my family happy. In fact, the kids laugh at me, they say when I tell a joke it’s not funny and then they start laughing, then I said, if my joke is not funny, why are you laughing?
It's more about happiness and watch the children grow, the grand children grow, to see their happiness, to see their progress, to see their development and how they get attached to you and the grand children come to want to be only with you.

Upsound:
Love you bye

Lourensa:
How do you control your emotions when you go on these responses and you meet these communities and you see the sadness in the world?

Dr Sooliman:
God has given me a special gift, it doesn’t move me. I don’t get attached to any situation. And I tell my teams before they leave, I said, feel for the situation, don’t feel for the individual.

VO: 00:08:34.18
Given what Dr. Sooliman has seen, he remains optimistic about South Africa’s future.





Dr Sooliman:
I'm a disaster tourist, I don't visit countries in good times, I go in the worst of times and I've seen real havoc… we are nowhere near that.

Link:
After having spend some time with Dr. Imtiaz Sooliman, I've learnt that it really doesn't take much to make a difference, we just need to look around us and start somewhere.

Dr Sooliman
As long as we participate within the country, we will fix the system. And you can see it already. People are saying, “we’ll fix the oceans, we’ll fix the potholes, we’ll cut the bushes on the side”. We do have problems, not something that we can’t fix. And the most important thing is active citizenry. The country does not belong to the government. Let's go back to the 27 April 1994, it is the single greatest event in our country. Not because a black government to replace the white government. We were told, fill your houses with food, nothing happened. Everybody was calm, peaceful, voted. But in nothing that happened, actually, everything happened. They said in their action, we are going to rebuild this country. If we haven't learned from that, sorry, we haven't learned anything.

We started off with the disasters and then gone into infrastructure hostage negotiation development. Maybe tomorrow I'll be doing something on electricity.

4: 21” Promo
VO: They say some superheroes don’t wear capes…
UPSOUND: Open doc and the foundation came along place orders need for us to really support the vulnerable children
VO: And few people know this better, than the men and women who’ve been assisted by Dr Imtiaz Sooliman and the Gift of the Givers…

5: 21” Promo
VO: From helping the displaced in war torn Syria, to bringing relief to the distressed in KwaZulu Natal and the Eastern Cape, for Dr Imtiaz Sooliman and his team at Gift of the Givers - there’s no place on earth that’s too far…
Dr Sooliman
I've never went around looking I'm gonna today I need to find something to do I don't have to just keeps coming.


On Camera 11’ Promo
Promo 1: Join us for an inspiring look at the man behind Gift of the Givers - Dr. Imtiaz Sooliman. His incredible achievements will astound you! Don't miss this inspiring story.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Not your average NGO, this is the largest disaster response organisation on the continent.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: An intimate look at Dr Imtiaz Sooliman, the founder of Gift of the Givers
metadata.Summary: Treatment Overview Opening and setup: 2 minutes We start the insert with a collection of disasters, wars, earthquakes and water shortages. From there we go into a link - we hold the audience in suspense - we explain where we are. In Pietermaritzburg. The reason why we visit a seemingly ordinary town is for an extraordinary individual. All will be revealed soon. Our presenter meets our hero. Dr Sooliman. Known for his NGO - Gift of the givers. We find ourselves in a warehouse. It’s massive. We conduct the interview in one of the main distribution centers of GOTG. We talk about Dr Sooliman’s history, from Potch to Maritzburg. Gift of the Givers: 4 Minutes Dr Sooliman is synonymous with Gift of the Givers. He has been all over the world, saving lives. Most recently, drilling hundreds of boreholes for the water crisis in the Eastern Cape. He talks to us about a variety of disasters his NGO was involved in. Lots of action and pace is fast. Then We find out GOTG is much more than we thought… We visit a school that GOTG built, the lives of children touched by the good doctor are evident here in a small school near Maritzburg. But there’s more… We also see a medical center they built, to help the less fortunate. We see Dr Sooliman talk at another unveiling of a ward at the Charlotte Maxeke hospital in Joburg… He is a very busy man. We cover a lot of these with photos. But then, we slow the pace again…. Faith: 2 Minutes All of what he created was through his faith. It is one of the most important pillars of GOTG. We see him in an intimate prayer session, in a mosque. We now have a better understanding of this unique individual. Dr Sooliman is one of the special ones. It takes someone like him to change the course of history. What would have happened to the people he saved, if it was not for him. Making the decision to start Gift of the Givers, in 1992, was life-changing. Closing: 2 minutes We wind it down as we look at what has been achieved by Dr Sooliman. And yet, he doesn’t care about the lifetime achievement award or the recognition he gets from the Presidency. Gift of the givers is all about the people of this beautiful country of ours.
metadata.Further information: Details of the insert I want to approach this as a mini doccie. To showcase Dr Sooliman. It won’t be a plight for donations or an advert for Gift of the Givers, just a look at the life of Dr Sooliman and his legacy. The audience will connect with him immediately, clearly a no BS person. Someone that acts. By the end of the insert, we will feel inspired and much more positive about our country. Dr Sooliman will take us on a journey of hope.
